title: Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV): The Pathophysiological Masterclass
summary: CNV represents the ingrowth of new, immature blood vessels from the choriocapillaris through Bruch's membrane into the sub-retinal or sub-RPE space. This clinical entity is a vision-threatening endpoint of various pathologies, primarily wet Age-Related Macular Degeneration.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: CNV is the proliferation of abnormal vessels derived from the choroid. Pathogenesis is driven primarily by Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF-A) upregulation. The sequence involves: 1. RPE/Bruch's membrane compromise. 2. Hypoxia-induced VEGF overexpression. 3. Angiogenesis via endothelial cell migration and proliferation. 4. Exudation of proteinaceous fluid and hemorrhage leading to photoreceptor damage and disciform scarring.

rows: Inverted 'C' zone of atrophy, temporal to fovea
Orange-red subretinal mass, 'lighthouse' effect on FFA

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Referral
content: Sub-RPE fluid causing elevation of the macula

sections.title: Diagnostic Protocol
content: Step 5: ICG Angiography (Required for PCV/Choroidal lesions)

sections.title: Treatment Algorithm
content: Dosing: Monthly for 3 months, then 'Treat and Extend'
Laser: PDT (Visudyne) - reserved for polypoidal/non-responsive cases
Surgical: Submacular surgery (rare, mostly for massive hemorrhage)

content.explanation: Aflibercept (Eylea), Ranibizumab (Lucentis), Faricimab (Vabysmo), Bevacizumab (Avastin - off-label but effective)

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: OCT-A is now the primary screening tool for non-invasive CNV detection.
Always check the fellow eye; AMD is inherently a bilateral disease.
Faricimab offers dual pathway inhibition (VEGF and Ang-2), potentially extending injection intervals.
Type 3 CNV (RAP) responds poorly to anti-VEGF compared to classic Type 2 membranes.
